summary: The accepted predecessor fact is used exactly to obtain the finite positive balancing family and individual cap bounds. Inclusion minimality yields affine independence and fresh positive barycentric weights; the shear has the correct sign, preserves every base fiber and the mixed measure, and therefore preserves depth. The R=0 branch, both score inequalities, all Markov thresholds and constants, fiberwise boundary-nullness, the cross-color midpoint argument, and both positive-volume and zero-volume Brunn-Minkowski cases are correct. The claim explicitly stops before the unproved global colored expansion-or-rank-drop bridge.
